Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for sending over the latest order form redlines. Quick note from our side on the IP/indemnity carve-out you requested. I want to make sure we understand the exact trigger you need for the carve-out so Legal can map it to obligations and commercial exposure.

High-level ask we saw: Acme wants the limitation of liability cap to explicitly not apply to claims arising from IP infringement caused by models used to serve your requests (you flagged concerns around third-party models and pre-trained artifacts).

Can you confirm: is Acme seeking a broad exception for any infringement claim tied to outputs generated by any model the customer selects (including third-party open-source and vendor models), or is this limited to claims where Redwood itself supplies the model and the infringement arises from Redwood-provided model artifacts?

If you can confirm, it will help us propose precise language. Briefly: Redwood is open to narrow carve-outs tied to Redwood-supplied models or where Redwood made model changes that caused the issue, but a broad uncapped exposure for all third-party models is a different risk profile and likely requires tailored pricing, proof/evidence obligations, and insurance/escrow mechanics.

I've attached our current redlines (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a short evidence checklist we use for IP incidents (Exhibit-A_IP-evidence-guidance.docx).

Suggested next step: 30 min call with Procurement + Legal to align scope — happy to schedule for this week.

Best,

Sofia —

Thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the materials. To clarify Acme's position (from Legal): we need an express carve-out to Redwood's liability cap for IP claims where the alleged infringement is tied to outputs delivered to Acme users via the Redwood service, regardless of whether the underlying model is maintained by Redwood or a third-party vendor. Our concern is operational: we rely on your runtime and model catalog to serve content; if an output infringes a third party's IP, we need the indemnity protection without having to separately sue the third-party model owner.

Proposed carve-out language (for consideration):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing limitation of liability, the liability cap shall not apply to any amounts payable by Redwood in respect of indemnity obligations arising from third-party claims that the Service outputs delivered to the Customer infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, provided that: (a) Customer promptly notifies Redwood of the claim; (b) Customer provides reasonable cooperation and the evidence described in Exhibit A; and (c) Customer does not modify the allegedly infringing output after receipt."

We included redlines to the Order Form indicating the insertion point. We understand Redwood may ask for commercial mitigations (higher per‑claim cap, insurance, or carve‑out limitations). Please let us know Redwood's position and suggested alternative wording if you cannot accept the proposal as written.

—Elena
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloud

Folks —

Read Acme's proposed language. High-level internal take: we can accept a narrow carve-out but not the open-ended formulation Acme provided. Key risks and suggested guardrails:

- Scope trigger: we should accept carve-out when the alleged infringement arises from outputs generated by Redwood-owned models or from models Redwood hosts with modifications made by Redwood that materially caused the infringement. We should avoid an uncapped obligation tied to any model the customer selects from our catalog (many of which are third-party open-source or vendor partners).

- Evidence and mitigation: require submission of Exhibit A items (raw prompt + output, dataset provenance where available, timestamps, sample user IDs), plus a technical reproduction attempt that we can run in our environment.

- Financial exposure: if we agree to a carve-out, propose a higher per‑claim cap for these IP indemnity payouts (e.g., USD 250,000 per claim) that sits above the general contract cap but below uncapped exposure. Alternatively, require primary commercial insurance placement for the event.

- Remediation & control: Redwood must retain the right to remediate (replace or remove) the model/project that allegedly caused the infringement and to defend settlements. If the customer modifies outputs post-delivery in a way that causes the claim, that should void the carve-out.

Draft compromise wording for internal review (high level):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), the liability cap shall not apply to amounts payable under Redwood's IP indemnity for claims alleging that outputs directly generated by Redwood-owned or Redwood-hosted models (where Redwood materially modified the base model) infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, provided that Customer: (i) promptly notifies Redwood; (ii) complies with the evidence obligations in Exhibit A; and (iii) does not materially alter the output after receipt. Redwood's total exposure under this carve-out shall be subject to a per‑claim limit of USD 250,000 and customary cooperation and mitigation rights."

Requesting input from Pricing (Marissa) on whether we can support this exposure commercially and from Sales (Sofia) on whether the customer will accept a per-claim cap plus the scope narrowing.

Aditya
Deputy General Counsel | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Jordan / Priya / Elena —

Thanks for the clear language and for the patience while we reviewed internally. Quick summary of Redwood's commercial compromise proposal so your teams can evaluate:

Proposal summary (Redwood):
- Scope: Narrow carve-out to apply only when the alleged infringement stems from outputs directly generated by Redwood-owned models or Redwood-hosted models where Redwood materially modified the underlying model artifacts. This avoids uncapped exposure for every third-party model in the catalog.
- Trigger & obligations: Acme must provide notice and full cooperation per Exhibit A (raw prompts, outputs, timestamps, usage logs). Customer must not modify outputs after delivery.
- Financial limit: Per‑claim cap of USD 250,000 for payments payable under Redwood's IP indemnity that fall within this carve-out. This is in addition to the general liability cap structure (i.e., carve-out sits above general cap but is itself capped per claim).
- Remediation & control: Redwood to retain remediation rights (replace/remove model, defend or settle) and to coordinate with Acme before any public remediation.
- Insurance/escrow: If Acme prefers a broader scope, we can discuss a commercially priced insurance endorsement or escrow guarantee; this would be priced separately.

Next steps:
1) Elena — can you confirm whether Acme would accept the scope narrowing (Redwood-owned / Redwood-modified models) plus the USD 250k per-claim cap? If not, please identify which parts are unacceptable and why.
2) Priya / Jordan — if you accept, we'll circulate clean redline language to insert into the Order Form and aim for DocuSign the week of Mar 4.
3) Internal: Marissa — can you send a short note on required pricing uplift (if any) to support the 250k exposure? Laura — I'll need a final small set of contract edits for remediation and evidence timing.

Happy to run a 30-min legal + procurement sync tomorrow if helpful — otherwise we'll await Elena's note.

Best,
